proposal: The Mandate recommends reinstating the Trump-era ESA rules on critical habitat and critical habitat exclusions, delisting the grizzly bear and the gray wolf, ceding sage-grouse management to western states, limiting experimental population releases, and making ESA decision data public. It also recommends abolishing the USGS Biological Resources Division and says Congress should reform the Act.

Delist the gray wolf in the lower 48 states (Executive Order 14425 deadline for Interior's determination is about 2026-12-03; H.R. 845 and S. 1306 have not become law).

status_summary: Three ESA final rules are published. FWS and NMFS rescinded the regulatory definition of harm (published 2026-07-14, effective 2026-09-14), and FWS published two rules on 2026-07-21, effective 2026-08-20: one reinstating its own critical habitat exclusion regulations at 50 CFR 17.90 as finalized in 2020, and one ending the blanket section 4(d) option for newly listed threatened species. The exclusions rule matches one of the two critical habitat rule sets the Mandate names; the 2020 regulatory definition of habitat was not restored, and the November 2025 proposal to revise 50 CFR part 424 does not propose it and has not been finalized. No grizzly bear or gray wolf delisting rule exists. FWS reopened comment (through 2026-08-17) on revised 4(d) rules for the lower-48 grizzly listing proposed in January 2025, and the notice describes no delisting. For wolves, the House passed H.R. 845 on 2025-12-18 (211 to 204 per E&E News; the engrossed bill text on govinfo carries the passage date and directs reissuance of the 2020 gray wolf delisting rule, with no court review), a Senate unanimous-consent request on S. 1306 was blocked on 2026-08-04, and Executive Order 14425 (signed 2026-09-04) directs Interior to determine within 90 days whether the gray and Mexican wolf meet recovery criteria, to begin delisting or downlisting if they do, and to prepare a legislative recommendation to delist or downlist them. For sage-grouse, BLM's September 2025 notice proposed plan changes aligning with state programs, but jurisdiction was not ceded. No action was found on section 10(j), a triage program, ESA data release, or the USGS Biological Resources Division. Suits against the rules were filed in July and September 2026.

timeline.event: FWS and NMFS propose revising 50 CFR part 424 (listing, delisting and critical habitat designation), replacing several 2024 provisions with 2019 text; it does not propose restoring a regulatory definition of habitat and is not final.

The House passes H.R. 845, the Pet and Livestock Protection Act (engrossed text marked passed the House on 2025-12-18): within 60 days of enactment the Secretary of the Interior must reissue the 2020 final rule (85 FR 69778) removing the gray wolf from the endangered and threatened species list, and the reissued rule may not be challenged in court. E&E News reports the vote as 211 to 204.
FWS and NMFS publish a final rule removing the regulatory definition of harm from 50 CFR parts 17 and 222 (effective 2026-09-14).
Environmental groups and two tribes file two suits in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Washington challenging the harm rescission (filing day inferred from a 2026-07-15 report).
FWS reopens comment, through 2026-08-17, on revised section 4(d) protective rules for the lower-48 grizzly bear listing proposed in January 2025; other parts of that proposal are not reopened.

FWS publishes a final rule reinstating its FWS-only critical habitat exclusion regulations at 50 CFR 17.90 (effective 2026-08-20); a companion final rule the same day ends the blanket 4(d) option for newly listed threatened species.
Sen. Cory Booker objects to a unanimous-consent request by Sen. Ron Johnson to pass S. 1306, the Senate gray wolf delisting bill.

The President signs Executive Order 14425, which directs Interior to determine within 90 days whether the gray wolf and Mexican wolf meet ESA recovery criteria and to submit a legislative recommendation to delist or downlist them (published in the Federal Register 2026-09-10).
